S76.03.needs: a model that reads images and one that does not (the app does not label this)
S76.03.note: The warning fires on any switch from an image-capable model to a non-capable one, not only when an image is attached. No refusal or reroute of image turns was found in the extension code; the picker does not show image support.
steps: Press Cmd+Shift+P, type Code: Select Model, press Enter.
Click a model that cannot read images (the app does not label which models read images).
Look for the modal "Switch to ...?" whose detail says it "cannot read images you attach"; compare with Expected.
S76.03.where: Command Palette > Code: Select Model > pick a model that cannot read images while the current model can

labels.text: This model does not take a reasoning effort.

S76.26.note: The effort button is hidden while a reply streams; the picker does not say which models take effort.
steps: In the chat composer, click the button labelled Mode and reasoning effort.
Read the Reasoning effort group in the popover.
Click the model pill (Auto) and choose a model; reopen Mode and reasoning effort.
Compare: the group lists only the levels that model takes, or shows This model does not take a reasoning effort. when it takes none.
S76.26.where: Chat composer > Mode and reasoning effort button > Reasoning effort group

S76.28.note: Trimming or refusal of over-long requests is not visible in the app; the context figure appears only after a reply.
steps: Press Cmd+Shift+P, type Code: Select Model, press Enter.
Read the grey detail line under a model: its id, then N context and N output.
Close the picker, send a message in chat, then hover over the context figure in the composer.
Compare the tooltip text Context after the last turn with Expected and with the context figure from the picker.
S76.28.where: Command Palette > Code: Select Model (the N context figure), and the context figure in the chat composer after a reply

Compare the N output figure with Expected.

S76.32.needs: a chat whose route reports prompt-cache tokens (the app does not say which routes do)
S76.32.note: Whether routing chooses a model or route for its cache class is not visible in the app.
steps: Sign in, open a chat and send a message; wait for the reply.
Send a second message in the same chat and wait for the reply.
Look under the second reply for a line starting Prompt cache with reused or written token counts.
Compare with Expected; the line appears only when the reply reports cache tokens.
S76.32.where: Chat reply > Prompt cache line under the reply (after a second message in the same chat)

S76.34.where: No control of its own; routing refuses routes outside a region

S76.35.note: Searched apps/extension-vscode/src for retention; none found. Local privacy mode concerns network access, not retention.

S76.37.note: The picker shows no deprecated or retired label; a tester cannot see which models were removed without the registry.
steps: Press Cmd+Shift+P, type Code: Select Model, press Enter.
Scroll through every provider group in the list.
Compare the models listed with Expected: models whose availability is not live are left out of the list.

S76.38.needs: a session whose route locks some models (for example a signed-out or Free session)
S76.38.note: Per-route price, retention and cache class are not shown in the picker; route ranking is not visible.
steps: Press Cmd+Shift+P, type Code: Select Model, press Enter.
Scroll to the bottom and read the locked group headings.
Click a locked model and read the message that explains it cannot run on this session's route.
Compare the headings and message with Expected.
S76.38.where: Command Palette > Code: Select Model (locked group headings at the bottom of the list)
